title: Minimum Time to Break Locks II
summary: Bob needs to break n locks, each requiring a specific amount of energy as specified in the array strength, where strength[i] is the energy needed to break the i^th lock.
statement: Bob needs to break n locks, each requiring a specific amount of energy as specified in the array strength, where strength[i] is the energy needed to break the i^th lock. The sword starts with 0 energy and increases its energy by the current factor X each minute. After breaking a lock, the sword's energy resets to 0, and the factor X increases by 1. Determine the minimum time in minutes required for Bob to break all n locks and escape the dungeon.
constraints: strength has 1–80 positive values up to one million.
The sword factor starts at one and increases by one after every broken lock; energy resets after each lock.
Assign locks to factor positions to minimize the sum of ceiling(strength/factor).
hints: Each lock must be matched to one distinct factor position.
Build the complete lock-position cost matrix and solve minimum-cost bipartite assignment.
Use the Hungarian augmenting procedure on costs ceil(strength[i]/position).
Perfect matchings correspond exactly to lock orders, so the minimum assignment cost is the minimum escape time.
editorial: Perfect matchings correspond exactly to lock orders, so the minimum assignment cost is the minimum escape time.

tests.explanation: An optimal order breaks the locks in four total minutes.
Assigning locks to factors one, two, and three optimally takes five minutes.
